deferredTracks.mechanism: RSA 265-A:21, I operates notwithstanding RSA 651:5, and RSA 651:5, III opens with an express exception for it. The section was read at gc.nh.gov on 2026-08-06 and the clock runs from the date of conviction, not from completion of the sentence, which is different from every other New Hampshire conviction track. deferredTracks.mechanism: Any person convicted of a criminal offence which occurred between May 14, 2014 and July 1, 2015 while the person was 17 years of age shall be entitled to an annulment of that conviction upon application to the court. Annulment requests under the section are not subject to any filing fee. These are adult criminal convictions entered against people who were 17 during the window before New Hampshire raised the age of juvenile jurisdiction, so the records sit in the adult system and the relief belongs in ordinary adult scope. The section operates notwithstanding RSA 651:5, so the paragraph V bars and the paragraph VI whole-record rule appear not to apply, which if correct makes this the strongest relief in the state. The marijuana counting rules that live inside N.J.S.A. 2C:52-2 and 2C:52-3 are separately carried on those tracks, where they were read in the enacted text of P.L.2019, c.269, so nothing about the regrading analysis is lost by deferring this node.
deferredTracks.mechanism: The controlling review records three sub-mechanisms arising from the 2021 marijuana laws: immediate relief with no waiting period for simple possession, failure to make lawful disposition, being under the influence, paraphernalia and distribution or possession with intent to distribute of less than one ounce of marijuana or less than five grams of hashish; a three-year wait for distribution of one ounce to five pounds of marijuana or five grams to one pound of hashish; and sealing by operation of law for a specified set, being possession of six ounces or less and manufacture, distribution or possession with intent to distribute of one ounce or less of marijuana or five grams or less of hashish, with no petition and no fee. The review states that this is a two-strategy track that must be split in the product, because telling a participant to file for something the law already sealed wastes their time. deferredTracks.publicName: Whether Ohio clears some records automatically
deferredTracks.legalDesignRationale: The question this node records is answered, and the answer is no. Current Ohio law provides neither automatic sealing nor automatic expungement of an adult criminal record; every adult route is begun by the person's application or by a prosecutor's motion under Ohio Rev. Code section 2953.39 and is decided at the court's discretion; and the one automatic provision, section 2151.356, is juvenile and reaches no adult record. That determination was made from the operative text of every adult sealing and expungement section as it currently reads and from the Supreme Court of Ohio's own current enumeration of the adult route set, and it is recorded in the integrated decision record oh-automatic-sealing-current-law-reconciliation at terminal disposition resolved_no_automatic_mechanism_exists. The node nonetheless stays deferred, and that is the correct posture rather than a leftover. A negative finding creates no relief: there is no mechanism to model, so there is no output strategy to choose, no component to build, no destination to file at and no packet to generate. Deleting the node would be worse than keeping it, because the claim it answers is in wide circulation and the product must be able to answer it; a deferred node is exactly how this memo records a question that is real, answered and unbuildable. What changes is the participant-facing consequence, and it changes in the participant's favour: the screening answer moves from "the position is unconfirmed" to "Ohio has no automatic route, nothing is coming, and the ordinary routes are the only way". The screening action itself is unchanged, because the memo already routed that participant to the ordinary routes rather than leaving them waiting.
deferredTracks.mechanism: Settled, and settled as a negative. Current Ohio law provides neither automatic sealing nor automatic expungement of an adult criminal record. Every adult route in the Revised Code is begun by the person's own application or, in the single exception, by a prosecutor's motion under Ohio Rev. Code section 2953.39, and every one of them is decided at the court's discretion after a hearing at which the prosecutor is notified and may object. The one provision in Ohio law that seals without an application is section 2151.356, and it is juvenile: it directs the juvenile court to order immediate sealing in stated circumstances and reaches no adult criminal record. The determination rests on the operative text of every adult sealing and expungement section as it currently reads — sections 2953.32, 2953.33, 2953.321, 2953.36, 2953.39 and 2953.521, each of which conditions relief on an application or a motion — and on the Supreme Court of Ohio's own current enumeration of every adult rights-restoration and record-sealing route, revised June 2026, which contains no automatic one. It is recorded in full in the integrated decision record oh-automatic-sealing-current-law-reconciliation, whose terminal disposition is resolved_no_automatic_mechanism_exists. The secondary source the controlling review flagged — which described Senate Bill 288 as providing automatic sealing handled by the court and the Bureau of Criminal Identification and Investigation without petition or fee, with implementation ongoing — is not borne out. Senate Bill 288 modified and reorganized the sealing laws and extended them to records after a pardon, effective April 4, 2023; it created no automatic route.

destination.name: No adult automatic route exists
destination.detail: Nothing administers an adult automatic route in Ohio because there is none. The courts and the Bureau of Criminal Identification and Investigation act on the ordinary routes: the court decides an application or a prosecutor's motion, and the Bureau receives the resulting order and, on a conviction expungement under section 2953.32, retains a limited record for law-enforcement employment decisions. No agency clears an adult record on its own motion. The one automatic mechanism in Ohio law, section 2151.356, is juvenile and is administered by the juvenile court.

deferredTracks.legalDesignRationale: The review's decision is "Additional research required" with the output strategy recorded as unidentified, because it could establish that a subsection (1)(d) existed but not what it said. That answer does not produce a new route, because the two dispositions it covers are already the review's own Tracks 2 and 3, which are normalized in this memo as implementable tracks under this very subsection. So the slot is preserved as a deferred cross-reference node with no output strategy asserted, rather than either dropped or built into a third packet that would generate a duplicate motion for relief the participant can already obtain. deferredTracks.publicName: A felony that is now a misdemeanor
deferredTracks.legalDesignRationale: Additional research required, as counsel decided, and high value: it converts ineligible participants into eligible ones. Reading § 12-1.3-1(5) at the official source closed counsel's first build blocker — the definition and the 26 June 2024 effective date are confirmed verbatim — but the two questions that make the overlay usable remain open: which offences the General Assembly has actually reclassified, which needs a maintained list, and whether reclassification lifts the no-felony-conviction bar in the multiple-misdemeanor route or only recharacterises the target offence. The track is deferred, absent from runtime resolution and unreachable, with counsel's structure preserved and the statutory confirmation recorded.
deferredTracks.mechanism: Section 12-1.3-1(5) provides that 'misdemeanor' includes, but is not limited to, those crimes previously classified as felonies under law at the time the original sentence was imposed but reclassified by the general assembly as a misdemeanor in the interim, prior to the time the motion to expunge is brought. A participant whose old conviction was a felony when imposed but is a misdemeanor today is therefore treated as a misdemeanant for expungement purposes, which moves them from the ten-year felony wait to the five-year misdemeanor wait and may make them eligible for the multiple-misdemeanor route they would otherwise be excluded from by the no-felony-conviction condition. This is an overlay on the first-offender misdemeanor and multiple-misdemeanor routes rather than a standalone remedy, and it is separated here because it has its own authority, its own effective date and its own factual test.

deferredTracks.legalDesignRationale: Additional research required, as counsel decided. Reading § 23A-27-53 at the official source confirmed the mechanism and added two eligibility facts, but it did not answer the question that matters for record clearing: what record remains once the original charge is dismissed and the defendant stands convicted of the lesser ingestion or possession offence. The mechanism is a plea-bargaining structure rather than a record-clearing one, and its interaction with the arrest and SIS tracks is not established. The track is deferred, absent from runtime resolution and unreachable, with counsel's structure preserved.
deferredTracks.mechanism: After receiving a plea of guilty for a violation of § 22-42-5 or § 22-42-5.1 a court may, without entering a judgment of guilt and with the consent of the defendant, defer imposition of sentence and place the defendant on probation on terms that must include a drug and alcohol evaluation and any recommended course of treatment. If after one year the defendant has completed treatment and complied with all conditions, the court shall dismiss the § 22-42-5 or § 22-42-5.1 charge upon the defendant pleading guilty to ingestion under § 22-42-15 or possession under § 22-42-15.1. No person previously granted a deferred imposition of sentence is eligible for a second. A defendant is ineligible where aggravating circumstances exist as defined by § 22-6-11, or where the defendant is serving a sentence under the supervision of the executive branch.

deferredTracks.mechanism: The director of the Bureau of Criminal Statistics may authorize the destruction of information and records of: persons who are dead; persons seventy-five years of age or older unless a violation has occurred within the last ten years; incidents that are no longer considered crimes under the laws of South Dakota; and misdemeanor offenses whose final date of disposition occurred at least ten years prior to the authorized destruction date.
